# RX publication and delivery observation for the 30 Hz seek failure

This isolated module observes the next unresolved boundary after the exact PES
and successful TX-publication captures. It does not fix the same-HANDLE seek
failure or change the installed runtime. The fixed 30 Hz source, PES probe,
normal decoder lifecycle, deadlines and hardware guards remain unchanged.

Build from this task branch with `CRYSTALHD_PM_RESEARCH=1
CRYSTALHD_TX_NOTIFY_RESEARCH=1 CRYSTALHD_RX_NOTIFY_RESEARCH=1 W=1`.
The module identifies itself as `3.10.27-rxnotify1`. Research power limits remain
0/0 for the initial OFF comparison. Read the module-lifetime snapshot at
`/sys/kernel/debug/crystalhd-tx-notify/trace`; reading allocates only a host
snapshot and performs no device accesses. The original TX-only source/module
and all earlier failures remain preserved.

The new compile-time backend uses the existing RX receipt hook sites for
reservation, fire return, IRQ completion, completed byte counts, PIB parsing
and dequeue disposition. It does not enable the separate firmware-research
ARM/SEAL/READ ioctls. It neither walks descriptors nor changes packet fields.
The reservation key carries `(RxSeqNumber, pkt_tag, list)` on the caller's
stack, so a fast IRQ or recycled packet cannot redirect the fire-return record.
Packet addresses and capture epochs are opaque identities, never memory to
read at snapshot time. Sequence/tag/list may repeat after restart; readers must
also retain chronological START/context boundaries.

Only missing boundaries are added: the original picture-mailbox read, original
START response fields, actual RX metadata-write arguments/status, pre-doorbell
arguments, already-read RX IRQ/error words, ready-enqueue status, and the
existing statistics query's returned queue counts with copied host shadows.
There are no additional register/DRAM reads or writes, queue queries, firmware
commands, retries, pauses, or pointer traversal. Host shadows in a STATUS row
are separate observations, not an atomic device-state snapshot. The collector
adds CPU work and lock contention and may affect scheduling.

The W=1 module build passes. Actual observer/store/PicQ controls pass 24
checks with the default backend and 68 with the RX backend, each normally and
under ASan/UBSan. Existing affected RX metadata/fire, ownership/ISR and PIB
checks also pass normally and with sanitizers. Two test-harness preparation
failures (forward-declaration extraction and a test-only stack pointer lifetime
warning) remain preserved; neither changed the driver. Native acquisition is
not part of these device-free results.

## Record contract

The original TX events 1–7 and their meanings are unchanged. The RX build has
32,768 fixed records, each at most twelve 32-bit values. Full/invalid records
increment explicit dropped/invalid accounting; overflow cannot qualify a
complete observation. There is no IRQ allocation or dynamic growth. The header
adds `rx-notify=1 backend=existing-receipt-hooks fifo_queries_added=0`.

| Event | Values in order |
| --- | --- |
| 8 START | command sequence, delivery queue address, release queue address, host picture-delivery address, RX sequence, cached PicQ bitmap |
| 9 PICQ | mailbox address, actual returned bitmap, capture state before the ordinary update |
| 10 META | original write address, DWORD count, status, list, RX sequence, channel, Y descriptor low/high, UV descriptor low/high |
| 11 RESERVE | packet low/high, tag, list, RX sequence, channel, capture epoch low/high |
| 12 DOORBELL | register address, channel, list, RX sequence, tag; recorded before the original void write |
| 13 FIRE_RETURN | tag, RX sequence, list, from the immutable stack key |
| 14 IRQ_RAW | original interrupt word, Y error word, UV error word, list states 0/1 before ordinary handlers |
| 15 IRQ | list, completion status, IRQ-entry time low/high |
| 16 COMPLETE | packet low/high, tag, status, Y/UV done DWORDs and flags only on success, capture epoch low/high |
| 17 READY | local list and actual ready-enqueue status; no packet access after publication |
| 18 PARSE | packet low/high, tag, parser result, packet flags, metadata valid, timestamp low/high, picture number/flags, EOS trailer, format metadata valid |
| 19 DISPOSITION | packet low/high, tag, existing disposition: output 1, format 2, recycle-zero 3, repeated-last 4, repeated-two-back 5 |
| 20 STATUS | existing free/ready queue counts, PicQ shadow, capture state, list states 0/1, total captured counter |

COMPLETE success precedes READY publication and does not by itself prove a
user-visible picture. READY may appear after concurrent parsing because its
record is taken after the queue operation returns; timestamps are observation
brackets. PARSE is recorded at the acceptance hook, not at speculative parser
peeks. A false parser return with format flags is a format notification, not
necessarily a malformed PIB. Valid regular metadata supplies its actual PIB
timestamp; format metadata supplies its separately validated timestamp.
Invalid fields are zeroed in records rather than copied from a previous DMA.
No session-number field or descriptor inventory is added.

These records can distinguish an observed mailbox publication with no RX
admission, an admitted transfer with no completion, or completed bytes with
parse/disposition rejection. Absence of a new PicQ publication still does not
prove why firmware stopped producing pictures. No physical-DMA destination
readback, decoder-consumption, external-application compatibility, or release
qualification is implied.
